description: The reading half of the Instagram account: the comments on the client's posts, the answer that goes out with her yes, the lead that becomes a ticket, and the numbers the post creator writes with
client_copy: Lee los comentarios de tus posteos, te arma la respuesta para que la apruebes y te marca en el tablero a los que son clientes.
_comment: PUBLISHING IS NOT HERE AND IS NOT MOVING. `social/core/instagram.py` puts
a post on the account and this plugin reads what people say under it: two
halves of one connection, two plugins, because a client buys either one on
its own. What they share is the TOKEN, and they share it by name —
`engine.provide('instagram.token', ...)` — never by importing each other's
module: every enabled plugin's surface modules live in ONE sys.modules
namespace and load in CORE_PLUGINS order, so an import would be a bet on
who got there first. That is also why every module in here is prefixed
THE ENV IS THE SEED AND THE TABLE IS THE CURRENT TOKEN. IG_ACCESS_TOKEN
comes from the instance's secrets.env, which is outside the container: a
refreshed token is written into `instagram_account` and every Graph call
reads the table first. Before that, a refresh lived in one process's
os.environ and died with it, which is how a connection that refreshes
itself still expires after sixty days.
IG_USERNAME IS NOT AN ENV. It is a fact about the token, read once from
GET /me and cached next to it, and it is what tells the account's own
replies apart from a stranger's -- Instagram hands ours back nested under
the comment they answer, and an agent that read its own reply as new would
answer itself every fifteen minutes.
READING IS A FLOW AND NOT A LOOP. `flows/comentarios-instagram` ticks every
fifteen minutes, and a tick with nothing new is one tool call and one line
-- `fetch_comments` answers «Sin comentarios nuevos.» and the run ends. The
plugin copies the FLOW.md into workspace/flows/ when it loads if it is not
already there, and never overwrites: from the moment the file exists it is
the client's, hers to pause and the agent's to edit.
KNOWN LIMIT, DMs: instagram_manage_messages requires Meta's Advanced
Access even on the account's own owner, so direct messages cannot be read
or answered from here. Nothing in this plugin pretends otherwise, and the
reply to a lead invites them to write to the address on the brand file
instead. It is the one thing this capability does not cover and the
catalog row says so.
IT REQUIRES `approval` AND `kanban`: answering and hiding are outward acts
on a public thread and both are gated, which needs the approval plugin's
row, card and queue; and a comment that reads like a lead becomes a ticket
on the board, which is the kanban plugin's `create_ticket` with
source=instagram and the comment id as source_ref -- that pair is the
dedupe, so the same comment never opens two.
